claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys under low applied fields is governed by atomic-level homogenization.
The hysteresis of these alloys under low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles is governed by atomic-level homogenization.
Small additions of Cu or Ag enhance atomic-level homogenization in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Cu and Ag are FCC metals suitable for the proposed addition.
A representative controlled intervention is addition of 3 atomic percent Cu or Ag.
Greater atomic-level homogenization enhances the alloy's magnetic properties.
Adding Cu or Ag will increase the magnetocaloric entropy change relative to an as-deposited alloy without the addition.
Adding Cu or Ag will reduce hysteresis relative to an as-deposited alloy without the addition.
The predictions are limited to low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The predictions are expected to hold for FCC-metal additions up to 10 atomic percent.
The exact mechanism connecting FCC-metal addition to magnetocaloric improvement is not fully understood.
Failure of the FCC-metal-added sample to show both increased entropy change and reduced hysteresis relative to the unmodified control would falsify the hypothesis.
